utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and those assisting us just outside of this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ierace, before we -- and Ms. Pilipovic, before we continue the examination-in-chief of Mr. Kucanin, I think there are two issues we have to pay attention to. The first is that Ms. Pilipovic indicated yesterday that you would inform the Chamber about the view of the Defence relating to the expert report of Mr. Donia. Ms. Pilipovic, please tell us what your view is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the first issue that my learned friend raised on Wednesday -- or Tuesday, was the question of Berko Zecevic statement under 94 bis. I think that was the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's a misunderstanding, but please tell us what you would like to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. 94 bis, even if its modified form, presumes -- says that the party which wishes to call an expert witness needs to provide the statement. That is, we have the same provision even now after the amendments of December. The only difference is that previously the deadline was set, and that was the 21 days before the date when the witness would be expected to testify. So the disclosure of the statement or the document, report of the expert witness by the party which intends to call that expert witness, and the only difference being whether the Trial Chamber or the Pre-Trial Judge will prescribe the entire limit within which it needs to be presented. Now, my learned friend said that Rule 65 -- in line with Rule 65 ter, it is said in the submission of my learned friend that this is an expert witness but the analysis was not disclosed, nor was it said last time that he would be an expert, and that is why the Defence objects to call Berko Zecevic on the date proposed by our learned friends because we had not been provided with the report of the expert witness, nor were we informed that he would be testifying as an expert witness. So these are the two reasons for our objection against his testimony on the date suggested by our learned friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you like to respond right away or would you rather do it later today?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you allow me a minute, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have some difficulty in understanding the two bases of the objection, but I think one of them as to whether there has been timely disclosure. Mr. Stamp will respond in relation to that ground now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours. The objection is based on the timing of the disclosure. Subject to correction from friends, but my record indicates that the relevant report was disclosed to the Defence on the 8th of June, 2000, and it was again disclosed to the Defence on the 26th of November, 2001. I don't know if that accords with the records of my learned friends, but these are the records that we have, that the documents were disclosed two years ago and also last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, let's check on whether this is correct or not, but it's my understanding that the objection is based upon the fact that whether the report has been disclosed or not, that it was not clear to the Defence that this would be presented as an expert witness, and they assumed, as far as I understand, that it would be an ordinary witness or -- well, of course we have not received these documents, so it's difficult for me at this moment to assess whether this is right or not. Do I understand you right, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you do, Your Honour. I have to report that the Defence has not received the expert report of that gentleman, Mr. Berko Zecevic, whom the Prosecution wishes to call as an expert witness. We only have his statement as a witness, only his witness statement, not his expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it should be a simple matter to clarify during the course of the day, the date of disclosure of the report upon which the Prosecution relies as expert evidence, so we will confirm the date and advise the Trial Chamber accordingly. On re-reading my friend's objection, I think I understand the second objection to be that she assumed, under the old Rule, there would be at least 21 days notice. If that's the case, then my response is that the new Rule came into being in December and that overrules the old Rule. There is a further issue which I understand to be that the witness has not been previously identified as an expert. That takes us back to the text of the 65 ter summary. The first sentence of that summary is: "This witness, a mechanical engineer, is a highly-qualified expert in heavy weapons technology." And it continues on from there. The next -- the third sentence is: "He will testify about the operation and effect of the 120-millimetre mortar round," and goes on from there. So I say that the Defence is on notice that this witness is "a highly-qualified expert" and would give certain expert evidence. The title of the 65 ter summary did not identify him as an expert witness, and that's why I raised the issue the other day, so there would be no misunderstanding, and invite my friends to respond. But under the new Rule, we have not breached any time constraint imposed by the Rules. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I first of all invite the parties that perhaps during the breaks today, whether they could achieve some kind of a settlement. I mean, it's all a matter of time, as far as I can see. I mean, even if there would have been some misunderstanding as to the quality of this witness or expert, I mean, this finally could not exclude him from giving evidence in this courtroom, I mean, just on the basis of that. So may I invite the parties to see whether they can reach whatever agreement so that we don't have to give complex decisions on whether newly adopted Rules are also valid for those documents that have been disclosed before or that the time of -- the moment on which the Prosecution indicates that they would like to present a report as expert evidence would be decisive. I mean, of course, as all professional lawyers, we could spend days and days on that, but I prefer to see whether the parties can reach an agreement on when this witness or expert report will be presented as part of the Prosecution's case, so that there would be a fair opportunity to cross-examine either on the basis of the report or on the testimony of the witness given in court. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I see that you realise what is at the core of the problem. On the 29th of October, my learned friend, under Rule 65 ter, disclosed the summary of the statement, but it was not said that it was an expert witness. The fact that it says in the text that he is an expert does not mean that he can also be examined as an expert witness. Besides, at that time we had the unamended 94 bis, and then it was said that the party wishing to call an expert witness will disclose within a certain time limit; and then secondly, within 14 days the opposing party needed to say whether it accepted the report or whether to cross-examine the witness, and I think that our learned friends did not act in accordance even with the previous 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I invite you to find a solution for the problem. If, Ms. Pilipovic, if it would be the position of the Defence that because, as you explained, Rule 94 bis would not have been observed properly by the Prosecution and that therefore the expertise could not be admitted into evidence, then I'd like to know, because then we'll have to give a decision on that. But if that's not your position, I'd like you to discuss the matter with the Prosecution and see what solution as far as the time and the preparation of cross-examination is concerned could be found. Yes? So I'll then close this issue for the time being, and I promised you that I would give you a decision on the pre-marked map we discussed yesterday. If the objection of the Defence on the admission into evidence of the pre-marked map would be solely based on the fact that the Defence would have had no opportunity to be present while the map -- or while this document was marked, it would have been denied, since documents that have been drawn, like sketches or markings on photographs or on maps, as we've seen many of them in this trial. So if these documents marked by a witness while giving a statement to the investigators of the OTP, these documents may be relevant and they may have probative value, and therefore they will usually satisfy the basic test of Rule 89(C). The claim that such documents would only be admissible as evidence once they were produced in the presence of Defence counsel finds no basis, neither in the Statute or in the Rules. Of course, the Defence may cross-examine any witness whose testimony relates to such exhibits on the content of such an exhibit and also on the way the exhibit was produced, and of course the Defence may also present any relevant evidence in relation to the content of such documents or on the documents themselves when the Defence is presenting its case. In this particular case, however, some doubt has been raised as to the relevance of the markings on the map the Prosecutor seeks to be admitted. The witness has testified that most of his investigations of incidents involving casualties were performed between August 1994 and December 1995. He also testified, on the other hand, that the knowledge of sources of fire that he marked on the map were known to him already during the time relevant to the indictment, that is, from September 1992 until August 1994, based on the results of his own investigations and those of his police colleagues. The Defence has put forward that the statement mentioned by the Prosecutor which the markings of the maps would be based refers frequently to the investigation of incidents that took place after August 1994. All together, there seems to be a dispute as to the relevance of the markings in relation to the statements. In this situation of at least some confusion as to the relevance, the Chamber prefers that a blank map would be used while examining the witness so that we can have full control on whatever relevance issue that might be raised. Mr. Ierace, I asked you to prepare for both situations. I'm certain you will have done so. So it's now time, I think, to ask Mr. Kucanin to be brought into the courtroom again so that you may continue your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst that's done, earlier you referred to the testimony, the expert testimony of Robert Donia. That, of course, is a matter that has to be dealt with under the Rules, so perhaps sometime in the next few days the Defence could indicate its position under Rule 94 bis in respect of that evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The time limit has not been lapsed, as far as I can see. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning and thank you for the decision that you took. This brings us to another request, namely, very exceptional possibility with regard to this witness to be allowed to examine this witness jointly by my colleague and me, given that Mr. Ierace and his colleague could take the floor previously. We should like both to examine this witnesses. We will be testifying more about sniping than about shelling on the one hand, and on the other, the Defence is once again placed in a position from which it cannot get out. I will indicate this to the Chamber. I am pointing only one of the example, which perhaps will help us not to waste time. I received from the Prosecution some documents which have the following numbers, and I will give them slowly for the interpreters and for the transcript: 00269222A, 226 is the last one. These documents have to do with two shells fired about which the witness testified yesterday. However, it is not only that these documents are mutually confounding, but you will see that the first document, which is 222, has -- refers to a shelling incident of 3493, and the second one has to do with an incident which is 30 -- 43093, but it has the same number. I have the photocopy for this now. The photograph which we received concerning one of these incidents is this one here. It is impossible, Mr. President, with a photograph like this, to once again -- to use this, and we are showing you because nobody knows what is provided in this information. When we have information like this, we are wasting the time. And I am placing it at the disposal of the Chamber. We need to re-organise ourselves, and that is why we are asking now to conduct jointly the cross-examination, on the one hand, so that we can prepare for it; and secondly, during the break, Mr. Ierace and myself could check what happened with this document, which we are quite -- that we are -- so that we make sure that nothing has been -- no, not hidden from us, but withheld from us, because if this is the photograph which is showing a possible military target in that area, I do remember the witness, while testifying yesterday, of course, this photograph requires particular importance. Thank you very much for your attention, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ask already for a copy which is not just black and white, but in the true sense of the word to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I admit, I did not dare comment at 3.00 in the morning. However, I will do it the next time, because it was -- when I looked at these elements yesterday and when we were faced with the text and we thought that the text was the same in both situations. And that was something that we realised too late, because we had other photographs which are more clear. However, we did not check the numbers, whether the same text there were other photographs. It is only last night that we discovered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The dedication of both Mr. Piletta-Zanin and Mr. Ierace to their case makes me to assume that, if necessary, you would make the phone call at 3.00 at night and Mr. Ierace would be glad to receive it at 3.00 at night. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would just add, Mr. President, that we have invited the Defence to inspect any documents they wish to which we have given them copies of, and we received no response to that. It would be more appropriate, I think, before my friend raises those issues first in court, that he approach us to at least see the original and see if it's any better than the blank copy that he has received, or at least invite us to check that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just make one general remark. First of all, the Prosecution could pay proper attention that photographs are not just black boxes if they are disclosed to the Prosecution -- to the Defence. And the Defence, if they receive a black box, as we all know, in black boxes, you don't know what is in it, could first of all address the Prosecution and not spend any time on it in Court, but after they've asked for clarification. I think then, Mr. Usher, we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just wanted to know whether we could cross-examine the witness together, jointly, and I haven't received the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will decide at the very moment where you could start the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I do understand that you can hear me in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, may I remind you that you gave a solemn declaration yesterday and that you are, during the whole examination, you are bound by that solemn declaration. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be given a copy of P3658. I have six copies at the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since it might facilitate the preparation of the Defence, the Chamber has decided by now that you will be allowed to cross-examine the witness, but not simultaneously, but one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace, as soon as we're ready with the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, yesterday you said that your investigations were confined to impacts from both sniping and shelling, which affected civilians rather than military people. I'd like you to mark some particular positions on the map in front of you. Firstly, in relation to shelling, you also said yesterday that you developed, through your investigations, an understanding based on ballistics analysis conducted by ballistics experts in the police service of the source of shelling fire, especially repeated sources of shelling fire. As you look at the map, and perhaps starting at the top right-hand corner, I'd like you to mark those places. But firstly, please keep this in mind: Please only mark places which you knew to be sources of shelling fire between September 1992 and August of 1994. Would you please mark the first position with the letter A, starting in the top right-hand corner. And perhaps first of all you could point to it and tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the village of Mrkovici, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you excuse me for one moment. Might I have access to the map which the witness has in front of him? Thank you. Might that be returned to the witness. I simply wished to check, Mr. President, that there were no pre-markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever it comes to marking of names of villages or streets, would it be a suggestion that as soon as the name appears on the map, that the party indicates on what location it is. For example, if I look at the first village indicated by the witness, which is in the right top corner, is Mrkovici, that we just say where it is written on the map M1 and 2, for example. It's quite a clear map and it saves us a lot of marking and -- so whenever the name is on the map, that we just indicate in what part of the map it is, using the numbers and the letters on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place with a blue marker the capital letter A alongside Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, having regard to my earlier question, you knew that to be a source of shelling fire during the period of time that I earlier mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did the shells land in that period of time that you understood to be fired from that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shells fell in the upper part of the town, in the Stari Grad municipality and the Centar municipality. One of them hit the Markale market in February 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving further around the map, what is the next area that you come to, perhaps moving around and to the right, if there is any area you know which is not on the map, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here on the right side, behind number 4 should be the location which is called Burije. However, I cannot see it on this map. But it is situated somewhere near number 4 that I'm pointing now with my marker. The name of the place is Burije, and that's where the town was targeted from with heavy artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a capital B alongside number 4.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And continue to make your way clockwise around the map to the next relevant point.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Trebevic mountain is here. It is overlooking Sarajevo. And this part here to the right from Zlatiste is sometimes referred to as the south-western side of the hill. As far as I know, there were several positions here from where the upper parts of the old town were targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, please place a capital C.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, that is in the region of N8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you draw a line around the relevant part of the slope of Trebevic. I think you said it was the south-eastern part.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this part here. Do you want me to draw a line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another location from which projectiles came and hit the town, as far as I know, is located on the slopes of Trebevic, and it is called Zlatiste. It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The spot that I'm pointing with my marker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a capital D in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, that is M8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any particular villages in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were any around Zlatiste. There was a barracks called Bosut, a Serb army barracks which was situated in the vicinity, and it was from that barracks that shells came. But I don't know about villages. I know that the MUP had a recreational centre there before the war which was taken over by Serb forces and converted into a military base, which then constituted a serious danger for the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue to move in a clockwise direction along the map. What is the next source of shelling fire in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slightly above Zlatiste is the village of Miljevic, which was also a notorious place, because it was an artillery emplacement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given its proximity to D, could you please mark that capital D with a small 1 alongside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, I think that is L8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also in the vicinity there was a village in respect of which we received information that its name was Petrovici. However, I'm not sure that that was the name of the hamlet, so I should not perhaps refer to it as Petrovici. However from what I know, and from intelligence received, it was from this area. However, I don't want to speak about it, because I'm not sure. Let me move to the area of Vraca. Which is situated right above the Grbavica neighbourhood, which was occupied by Serb forces. There was a MUP school which was located at Vraca, which used to belong to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but which was taken over by Bosnian Serbs at one point in time. It was a very important stronghold for them and it was from there, from the vicinity of the MUP school that fire was opened. At one point in time, professors and students of this school were held captive in this school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, I think you're referring to J7. Just before you mark that, are there any other areas which appear on the map which were known to you in that period as a result of your investigations and the investigations of your fellow inspectors to be a source of shelling fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before Vraca or here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything further south of Vraca that fits that description, that is, further down the map, towards the bottom of the map. I direct your attention to further down the map, that is, in a southerly direction, perhaps west -- or east of the airport, due east of the airport.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not an expert, as I told you. East of the airport, do you mean this area here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll leave that for now. Perhaps we'll go back to Vraca. Would you mark the area you earlier indicated with the capital letter E.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if I may just interrupt you. When the witness's testimony was about Vraca, you indicated that he was pointing at J7. He is marking -- and as far as my recollection goes, he also pointed at K7.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Mr. President. It is K7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to Vraca, what type of fire emanated from that area? At this stage I'm not talking about sniper fire, but mortars or shells of some description.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both mortar, artillery, and gunfire came from the area of Vraca. As I indicated, it was one of the most important strongholds of the VRS situated close to the town, as you can see. Right in front of it there is the very centre, the very heart of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area right above the neighbourhood of Dobrinja, there is the hill of Gavrica, the Gavrica hill. However, I cannot locate it on this map. However, I know that the entire area of Dobrinja was shelled from artillery pieces from this position. I think that it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, I think that's I9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place a capital F in that position, and we understand that you cannot be precise about the location when you do so.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vicinity of Dobrinja I, there used to be a church, if my memory serves me right -- the name was Meljine -- from where the neighbourhood of Dobrinja was targeted from mortar pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place a G in that position.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think that is H9, approximately. What type of church was it? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: An Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of non-sniper fire came from that source?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that it was known as Meljine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the spot that I'm indicating right now is the area of Nedzarici, where a VRS military barracks was located, and it was from this location that this part of the town was shelled, that is, the Alipasino Polje and Alipasin Most areas, the Alipasin bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place a capital H on that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, it is F8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this spot here, there used to be a forestry training or school centre, from where the free parts of the Ilidza municipality, Sokolovic Kolonija, and Hrasnica, were targeted from artillery and mortar pieces, including the Igman road, which was used for bringing in food and other supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that position with a capital I.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the record, I think that's C10.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in this area, right above the village of Ahatovici, towards the end of the map, there is a flat land, a plateau, called Paljevo, from where the entire lower part of the town was shelled. The Rajlovac area, Buca Potok, all civilian, purely civilian areas, and other lower parts of the Sarajevo town. From my investigations where civilians were the victims, I know that the projectiles came from this area. I don't know the word -- I cannot see the word "Paljevo" here on the map, but I know this area was called Paljevo. I used to live nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your ability, could you place a capital letter J in the position of Paljevo. And I appreciate you have some difficulty in locating it precisely.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A2, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area here, there is the village Krivoglavci, situated near the municipality of Vogosca. It is from this location that mortars shelled the free parts of the municipality of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a capital letter L -- I'm sorry -- K in that position.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you state the name of that village again, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krivoglavci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map, I don't see the part situated right above Vogosca. You see the word "Vogosca" here. However, what's lacking is Blagovac, which was a notorious stronghold from where fire was opened from tanks and mortar pieces on the free parts of the Vogosca municipality, including Kobilja Glava. The location is slightly behind this spot here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a capital letter L off the map in the approximate area.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area is called Poljine. It is a wider area comprising several places, from where the centre of Sarajevo was targeted from various artillery pieces. That is the areas around the Kosevo stadium Kobilja Glava, the city cemetery and also the road which lead here through these neighbourhoods which are linked with the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you're pointing at this stage, I think, to a position on the map of K1; is that correct? All right. Would you please place a capital letter M on that position.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that that was a source of fire from various artillery pieces. What about mortars?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this -- oh, you mean at Poljine?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. I meant mortars too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And somewhere here, where I'm pointing, that is where Kromolj is. I mentioned it yesterday. And from it, both artillery and sniper fire was opened at this part of the city near the Kosevo stadium and neighbourhoods of Bare, Breka, and this area here which links the neighbourhoods of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place an N in that position, and that's L2 on it's map.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, what about the barracks at Lukavica? During that period of time, did you or any of your fellow investigators establish a source of shelling fire or mortar fire as being the Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There are the Rajlovac and Lukavica barracks. The two barracks where the army of Republika Srpska was quartered, and in Lukavica they had heavy artillery. And from Rajlovac they razed to the ground a locality called Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you've already marked the Rajlovac barracks as K. Would you please mark the Lukavica barracks with the letter O.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I think that's J10 for the record. I'm sorry. Yes, J10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kucanin, are there any other sources of shelling fire which are relevant to that particular period of time that appear on the map, or have you marked those which you knew from those sources of information?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mark the Rajlovac barracks, and it's here. And all the neighbourhoods along the railroad tracks and the road, I mean, all the civilian neighbourhoods were at peril, at risk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You marked the area with the letter K. That was, I think, the village of Krivoglavici. Would you mark the barracks at Rajlovac with the letter P, capital P.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other sources of shelling fire for that period that you haven't marked on the map, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, often mention was made of Biosko and the area about Faletici. If you follow it closely, Sarajevo is in a hollow and it is surrounded by hills, and from many of these hills, I mean, it was easy to place mortars or whatever and open fire because the city was down there as if in the palm of your hand. All the targets were quite visible. You could spot every single person that was there, so fire could be opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you now please return to the north-eastern corner of the map, that's the top right hand section. I will invite you to do the same exercise moving in a clockwise direction in relation to sources of sniping fire that were identified from either your investigations or those of your fellow investigators in the same period of time. What is the first such position as you move clockwise around the map from the north eastern corner?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first such position is the ill-famed hill called --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must object to this question, because it refers once again to hearsay. What I see from the text, the question was as follows: "Identified from either your investigations or those of your fellow investigators," literally. I think that to examine this witness about the investigations of his fellow investigators does not seem either logical or acceptable to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as you might have noticed, the case law of this Tribunal does not forbid hearsay evidence to be presented. On the other hand, Mr. Ierace, the Chamber would very much like to know whenever the witness gives information, whether it is from his own investigations or from investigations of his fellow police officers, so that we are better equipped to assess the probative value of the testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, would you please look at the position A that you marked on the map. I think that was Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what source of information did you establish Mrkovici as a source of fire during that relevant period of time? Was it from your own investigations or the investigations of your fellow investigators?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My own. But perhaps I can help by explaining this. We had investigating teams, and one investigator would be the leader investigator and he would be the one to draw up the report, the official note, and everything that had to do with that particular investigation. And then several of us would be the -- what shall I call us? The auxiliary staff, and we would all be helping this particular lead investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a two-fold problem. We have a spacial and a temporal problem, that is, not only one problem. We have a problem with space and a problem with time. We therefore need to know quickly when this witness speaks about his investigations, that he speaks about those prior to August 1994 or after that. That is, we must always pinpoint in time the knowledge of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also specify in your questioning the time in which the investigations took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did at page 23, line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree that you limited at that very moment to the period relevant to the indictment. So -- but perhaps I may please, then, remind the witness, then. Mr. Kucanin, when we are talking about your investigations, please keep in mind that Mr. Ierace started his questioning specifically asking you about the period of time September 1992 until August 1994. So if there's any source of knowledge, for example, investigations either made by yourself or under your supervision by fellow police officers, which are outside these time limits, would you please indicate this. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your investigations in that period of time, that relevant period of time of September 1992 to August 1994, what role did you play in your investigations? Were you the lead investigator or one of the auxiliary investigators?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the lead investigator in about 20 cases, and in about as many, perhaps, I would be the -- I was the assistant investigator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that Mrkovici was established as a source of shelling fire based on your investigations during that relevant period. What about position B, that is, Burije, which you identified as being slightly off the map?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not conduct any investigation to do with Burije, but my partner did that. I know that he conducted the investigation, and it was established that it had come from Burije.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's in the relevant period of time, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right. I am referring to that period only all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Position C, the south-eastern part of Trebevic, did that arise from your investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My investigations, because I conducted investigations in the upper part here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, apart from your investigations, was it established as a source of fire by other investigations in that relevant period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back briefly to Mrkovici, you've told us you established that as a source of fire from your investigations. Was it also established as a source of fire during that relevant period by other investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and repeatedly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to position D, that is, the area of Zlatiste, what is the position with that source of fire? In other words, in the relevant period, was it identified by you or by other investigators or by both?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both by me and by others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to position D1, the village of Miljevic, was that identified in the relevant period by your investigations, those of your fellow investigators, or both?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My fellow investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Vraca, that is, position E, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that, and my colleagues too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Position F, Gavrica Brdo. I'm sorry. Position F was -- could you please go to position F on the map. Which location is F?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gavrica Brdo. Gavrica hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the situation with Gavrica Brdo? In other words, was it your investigations or those of your fellow own investigators or both during the relevant period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period under investigation, I was assistant investigator on a number of occasions when investigations were conducted establishing that, and again, my colleagues did that even on those occasions when I wasn't a part of the team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Position H, that's the BSA barracks in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my personal experience and also my colleagues'. Yesterday I mentioned two cases that I handled, and on both of those occasions, the projectiles came from the direction of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Position I, that is, the forestry school?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I -- am I wrong when I missed G, or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, you're not wrong. That's my oversight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we go to the forestry school, position I, would you please go to position G.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My partner and I, as his assistant, did an investigation here, when the projectiles came from the direction of the church at Meljine. And may I address O, which is right next to it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Lukavica barracks, and I have personal experience from there and quite a number of my investigators conducted investigations here, establishing that the projectiles had come from the direction of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say quite a number. Do you mean by that, that was a stronger source of fire than some of the others you have mentioned, a more frequent source of fire, I should say?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a better word, "more frequent," yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And given the confines of the investigators' department, I take it you're referring to it being a source of fire where there were civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now go to I, that is, the forestry school, and tell us whether that was identified as a result of your investigations in the relevant period or those of your fellow investigators, or both.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, my vehicle was hit on the road, and I sustained a back injury. And we conducted the investigation. So it is from my personal experience that I can say when I was wounded, and it was established that the projectiles came from the school centre, and my other colleagues also conducting investigations establishing the same thing, the same source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of source was it? Was it a mortar round or an artillery shell or what?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft. I think it was 40-millimetre, the Bofors type, more or less, which is an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now go to J. That, I think, is the region Paljevo, on the top left-hand section of the map, where you had a little difficulty in identifying precisely where it was from the map. Is that from your investigations or those of your fellow investigators, or both, during the relevant period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period under consideration, it was my colleagues who did that. I didn't. I worked there at a later time, not during that particular period here. It was all my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next addition I think is K. Could you identify again the name of that area.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krivoglavci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the situation with the identification of Krivoglavci as a source of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues' report and from the police station at Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think the next area is the Blagovac hill; is that correct? That's L.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the situation with the identification of that source of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and my partner -- or rather, my partner was the lead investigator, but I worked there together with him, and there were two civilian persons, an adult and a child, in the neighbourhood of Barice, and we established that the projectile had come from the direction of Blagovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: M, that's Kromolj. I think M was Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Poljine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the situation with that, with Poljine being identified?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assisted in the investigation there on several occasions, and we established that the projectiles had come from the direction of Poljine. And the same holds true of Kromolj, marked with N.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And now we come back to the identification of the sniping sites. Would you go to the top right-hand portion of your map, and commencing from that position and moving in a clockwise direction around the map, could you take us to the sources of sniping fire that were identified by either you or your fellow investigators, or both, during the relevant period. And as you identify them, could you tell us which it was, whether it was your investigations or the others or both.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where I'm pointing now, is Grdonj, a hill called Grdonj, and Sedrenik is the area here. In between is the ill-famed Spicasta Stijena, the spiked rock, as they called them, and from there a sniper targeted the villages around, and many people were wounded here, and the old part of the city, the Kovacici one. I participated -- I conducted one of the investigations, and my colleagues performed many more such investigations there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, that's N3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described that as being ill-famed. I take it from your choice of words that it had a particular notoriety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so it is. So it is. I said that very many civilian casualties were there. It is a rock outcrop and it was very easy to target civilians from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving around the map, what is the next relevant position that you can identify?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where I'm pointing now, is a place called Osmice. After a hostel that was called that, and the road which sort of made that kind of bends, and that is why it was called. And from that place you -- the whole city could practically be controlled by the so-called Death Sowers, and the snipers and all types of other rifles. I think it was from this place and from Vraca, I think that from these two places the largest number of projectiles were fired at the city. I conducted several investigations there, and at least -- in at least one case I was the lead investigator, in some of them I assisted, and there were a number of cases also when my fellow investigators performed those investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, that is M7.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Time for one more, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have better expectation, as far as I can see, from how many numbers approximately might still follow. I promised everyone that I have a full break of half an hour, so I'm not stealing the time you need to recover from the first hour. If it would be five or seven minutes and if the interpreters' booth would agree, we could continue and then have a break until after 11.00, if there would be more, we perhaps better have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think we had better have it now, Mr. President. I have quite a few to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed under the guidance of our new registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President, and might I quickly update the Trial Chamber in relation to the two issues which arose this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin has kindly given me his copy of the blank photographs. We're making some inquiries about that and we are considering the feasibility of having Mr. Zecevic called at a later date so as to comply with the old Rule. I will provide the Trial Chamber and my learned colleagues with some further information on that tomorrow morning, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, we finished number 2 of the sniping sites, which was Osmice. Would you now identify, if there be one, the third site as you move clockwise around the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vraca region, the Vraca settlement, and also the part right above the Grbavica neighbourhood, which I'm indicating now, just before that area, there is the Jewish cemetery from where sniper fire was opened on the centre of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark that with the number 3 and inform us as to the source of information for the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both my investigations and my colleagues' investigations. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So from the Jewish cemetery towards Vraca, there's the settlement of Gornji Kovacici, though I cannot see the letters here on the map. But it is here, more or less, here where I'm indicating, in the same area, in this same square. I can see Kovacici; however, there's also Gornji Kovacici, where Serb army positions were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that with the number 4.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the source of information in the relevant period for the identification of number 4?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assistant investigator, and my colleagues did it. Other locations include a whole range of places: Vraca, the area of Vraca, which I could mark with number 5; up to the police school, the area that I'm indicating now, all situated in Grbavica neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Both me and my colleagues conducted onsite investigations in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify with a cross the position of the police school.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area leading from the Vrbanja bridge, which was on the other side of the Miljacka River, the one which was under Serb forces control, up to the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo bridge, that is, from here to there, this is the Grbavica neighbourhood, where there were a number of sniper positions which were active, and they were endangering this other area which was under the BH government control, which included several very important locations and facilities. There was a number of important buildings here: The Metalka company, for example, the skyscraper in Lenjinova Street, skyscrapers, and also a commercial centre here. That is the area, that is, these were the skyscrapers from which there was constant sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much of your -- I withdraw that. Approximately what percentage of your investigations were taken up with sniping from that area, that general area that you've just discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself worked on at least three such cases where trams were hit by sniper fire coming from these positions. I was assistant investigator on at least five onsite investigations conducted in this area here, which included killing of a French soldier and a number of incidents where French soldiers were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that French soldiers who were working for the United Nations at the time that they were killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they killed by sniper fire or shelling or a combination?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to have this incident becoming part of the record, because it's outside the time framework. However, I have to say that soldiers were very frequently targeted in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "soldiers were very frequently targeted," do you mean soldiers working under the banner of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please go back to the cross --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The witness has just stated that one of these incidents didn't happen within the relevant times. Could we be sure and certain -- could we make sure that all these incidents correspond to the relevant times, the incidents involving tram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness gave that evidence yesterday, but I'm more than happy to confirm it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, you've referred to you investigating three incidents involving trams being hit by sniper fire coming from the positions you have just identified. Did all of those three incidents take place in the relevant period or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked on at least three such cases. I participated in the onsite investigations which took place in that period of time, but I also worked on other incidents outside this time framework.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You made a point of telling us that the incident involving the French soldiers occurred outside the relevant time period. Would you continue to do that, please. In other words, confine yourself to incidents which occurred in the relevant time period, and if it becomes necessary to refer to incidents outside that period, please inform us of that fact. All right. Now, going back to the cross that you've placed on the map to indicate the police school, would you place a 1 alongside that cross.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a number of other sniping sites on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation line. You referred in particular to the building Metalka. Would you locate that on the map, please, and place a cross in that place with the number 2 alongside it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also referred to skyscrapers in Lenjinova Street. How many skyscrapers were there in that street from where sniper fire originated?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are four skyscrapers in Lenjinova Street which were affected by military activities. They are not accurately represented here. They're square in shape, and they are here, at the spot that I'm indicating right now, between the Miljacka River and Lenjinova Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the skyscrapers of uniform height?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many storeys, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in a line or some other geometrical pattern, that is, the four buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less in a line along the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please indicate their approximate approximate position on the map by drawing a line and then placing the number 3 alongside the line.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as to avoid confusion, would you place a circle around the number 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other buildings which were identified as a source of sniper fire in the relevant period as a result of your investigations or the investigations of other criminal inspectors or both?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three skyscrapers, referred to as shopping centre at Grbavica. Each of them had about 20 floors. They were very often used as firing positions. Targeted the centre of the town and Titova Street, and for a very long time, civilians were getting killed on this spot that I'm indicating right now. Although before there were some barricades had been set up in this part, as some kind of protection against fire coming from Trebevic, Gornji Kovacici, and some other areas. But it is from these skyscrapers that fire was opened, and civilians were targeted here. Later on, UNPROFOR placed a number of APCs and barricades on the spot. The approximate location of the skyscrapers would be here. I did not personally take part in any such investigation as a leader; however, I assisted my colleague when the person by the name of Jugoslav Komarica was killed. Somehow I remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that during the relevant period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the three skyscrapers in a row or in a different formation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly in a row. I cannot recall at this moment. They were on a square, or maybe a triangle. They formed a triangle, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place a triangle in the approximate position of the skyscrapers, and within the triangle, could you place the number 4.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that there was a particular site in the city where civilians were killed and where the fire was established as coming from those three skyscrapers. You said that a barricade had been placed on that site to offer protection, and I think you said that the position of the barricade, in fact, did not offer protection from the three skyscrapers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please mark the position in the city where the civilians were killed from fire coming from site -- the site of the three skyscrapers. If you could mark it with a cross, please, and the number 5 alongside it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was the direction of fire that the barricade initially was intended to protect civilians from?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the fire opened from these skyscrapers; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that initially the barricade was positioned to provide protection from a different direction, and it was discovered that it wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- protection from the three skyscrapers. So what was that first direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the area of Osmice and the Jewish cemetery, also from Gornji Kovacici. It is from these positions that the -- this road here was endangered. Trscanska Street and the civilians who walked along the street and also the street near the building of the supreme court and this other building. The barricade was set up in this way, in the way I'm indicating right now, in order to afford protection from sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the barrier on a particular intersection of Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the cross-street on that intersection?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street above was called at the time Djure Djakovica Street, and it led towards Skenderija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, just for the sake of the record, I think it's important that it is clear that the witness pointed as the previous lines of fire from those places indicated on the map by markings numbered 2, and later 3 and 4, in the direction of the cross with an adjacent 5 to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there a particular part of the city that was more prone to sniper fire than other parts in this general area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this area here, there was a part. It was called Trscanska Street and we called it Trscanska, or the "running street," because it was impossible to cross the street. So that's why we called it runners' street. The area was dangerous all the way up to the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo bridge. It was constantly exposed to sniper fire, and I think that dozens of civilians were victims of this fire. I assisted my colleague, Ilija Rosic, when a cyclist was killed in this incident from this Chanska Street up to the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo bridge. You see these letters here Novo Sarajevo, that's where the barracks of the former JNA was located, and it was one of the main streets leading to the lower part of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please use the marker pen to outline that part of the city which received that more intensive fire.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise on the map the three locations of the tram incidents that you personally investigated during the relevant period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One such incident occurred near this junction here. All of them occurred within a ten-metre diameter. One of them happened near the crossroads just below Trscanska Street. One occurred near the technical school, here, more or less; and one took place in the area of Pofalici, right before the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark those three positions with a cross and alongside the crosses place the numbers 6, 7, and 8.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also said in your earlier explanation about the three shopping centre skyscrapers that UNPROFOR placed some barricades in position to offer protection from that source of fire. Could you point to the place where UNPROFOR placed the barricade.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, right across the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So do I take it, therefore, that UNPROFOR placed a further barricade at position number 5 to offer protection from the three skyscrapers?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you continue to make your way around the map and identify any other positions that may have been identified in the relevant period by yourself or your fellow investigators. Sorry. Just before you do that, would you go back to the intersection marked 5, and if that could be shown on the ELMO. I'd like to ensure that we have a circle around that number 5. Would you place a circle around the number 5 on the intersection, so as to avoid any confusion at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now continue to point out the relevant positions.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may just add in connection with the location number 5: An investigating magistrate who conducted investigations lived here in the vicinity, and we discovered this location, that is, this firing position on the skyscraper, once when we came to fetch the investigating magistrate. We left the car here, we entered the building to pick up the judge, and when we came back, on the passenger's seat, we realised that there was a hole which was made by a sniper bullet. And as we went out, we realised that one part of the skyscraper was actually covering this area here, so we started paying more attention to the skyscraper, and then we invited UNPROFOR --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we ask the witness the exact date of this particular incident? I should like to know whether we are still within the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it needn't be entered in the record. I just wanted to tell you the way we discovered this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is not the first time that this witness is mentioning an incident which falls outside the scope of the relevant times. I don't want to have to be on my feet every time that the witness is mentioning an incident without giving us the specific time reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me just take you back to a decision I gave in the beginning of this day. One moment, please, so that I can quote myself without any mistake. The Chamber has expressed that it would prefer the marking on the map to be done in this courtroom in order to avoid any confusion as far as the relevance is concerned. That's what you will read on page 7. It seems that you misunderstand the decision of the Chamber, since the Chamber has not indicated that incidents which are not within the time limits of the indictment are, as such, irrelevant. They might be. We wanted to keep a tight control over any relevance question. From your observation, I do understand that you expect both the Prosecution and the witness not to refer, in whatever way, to whatever happened after August 1994 or before September 1992. As we have discussed during this trial at many occasions events that happened before especially September 1992, it might be clear to you that events may have relevance. So whenever the Prosecution would ask questions about the period after August 1994 or before September 1992, the Defence, of course, can raise an objection and ask what the relevance would be. But the mere fact that an incident took place after August 1994 or before September 1992 doesn't make the testimony in this respect irrelevant, but there would be perhaps a reason to ask ourselves what the relevance would be. So I think there's no reason to complain that you have to get on your feet now and then. If you want to raise the issue of relevance for any incident outside the period I just mentioned, then of course you may do so, and then we'll ask the Prosecution, if it's not clear of itself, what the relevance might have been. Otherwise the Prosecution will have to explain what the relevance of its question is, so just to avoid whatever misunderstanding. But I do understand that you make an objection as far as the answer of the witness is concerned relating to a moment which might be beyond the time scope of the indictment. Let me just confer with my colleagues, but first give Mr. Ierace the opportunity to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the explanation provided by the witness was volunteered; it wasn't in response to a question I asked. But it is still relevant because it explains the method by which sources of sniping fire were established, and therefore it does not matter whether this particular incident occurred within the indictment period or not, provided the technique was used during the indictment period. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I? Thank you. Merely to clarify. What the Defence wishes here, that Mr. Galic is here reproached with participating in a campaign based on a number of elements, and what we want is that in the transcript no possible confusion can be made, that whenever a witness speaks about an element outside the period, that it be registered then to say it was outside this particular time frame, and then we shall have nothing against it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that that's exactly what the witness, did, but let me just check. Let me just check, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I do agree with you, it was upon your question that the witness said it was outside the time limit, so you are perfectly right in making this remark. Mr. Kucanin, whenever you refer to what you experienced, and if it's outside the period of August -- September 1992 and August 1994, as you indicated upon the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin, your experience with fetching the magistrate, would you please also indicate whether it's outside the scope or within the time scope of September 1992, August 1994. Yes? Would you please ... this would assist us in knowing exactly when it happened. Mr. Ierace, please proceed. No. I still have to give a decision on the objection, although the last remark of Mr. Piletta-Zanin was not in support specifically of the objection any more. If Mr. Piletta-Zanin would not have asked our specific attention to the time frame, we would have said it to the witness as well. The answer the witness gave, not on a specific question, but explaining part of knowledge, has some relevance, both the relevance indicated by Mr. Ierace, that it might show how, what methods were used, and also, and I add that, that also outside specific investigations you could collect some information about the type of incidents he investigated at other times. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, in relating that incident so far, you have told us that after you returned to the car, you discovered a hole made by a sniper bullet on the passenger's seat, and as a result of that, you realised that one part of the skyscraper was able to cover that area. You also said that as a result of your observations, you started paying more attention to the skyscraper, and then you invited UNPROFOR to do something. What did you invite UNPROFOR to do?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first we told them that there was a sniper nest on one of the skyscrapers and that it was a threat to civilians, so whether they could do something to remove it. However, the UNPROFOR could not do it, but they instead brought some APCs, and I mean, to begin with, they brought the APCs, they put them across the street, at an angle, enabling the civilians to move there, and later on some containers were placed there to protect -- to shield the citizens from this particular sniper nest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you went to pick up the investigating magistrate and discovered the hole on the passenger's seat of the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
