utterances.text: It was in 1993. I'm quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long after that incident was it that UNPROFOR placed the APCs across the street and later some containers at, I take it, position number 5 with the cross?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a lot of time elapsed. I'd say not less than six months. That is, from the time when our windshield was broken by that bullet. These vehicles were placed there in daytime, that is, at the time of the most intensive traffic, so they had to be removed. And about a year passed by before some lasting shield was set up. And the citizens tried to somehow make do by themselves, so they would hang some blankets or sheets on a clothesline, or some wire, so as to protect them. So it took a year, about a year, to put the containers there to shield the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the only occasion that UNPROFOR was informed of a source of sniping fire against civilians and then action was taken by UNPROFOR in response to that information, or were there other times as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other times as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many other times were there during the relevant period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd say not less than 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue to move around the map and identify any other sniping sources of fire there may be as a result of your investigations and those of your fellow criminal inspectors in the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure. Here is Ozrenska Street. Now, about this, I heard it Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 4623 to 4629 from my colleagues who did investigations there. I did not participate in them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you please draw a line with the marker pen parallel to Ozrenska Street so that we can identify the street from the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place number 6 alongside that line.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep going, please, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is Zagorska Street. Yesterday we talked about one of the incidents when a boy was killed who used to live on Zagorska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place a blue line alongside that street and a number 7 at the top of the line.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please keep going.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is Milinkladska Street, but I learned about that from my colleagues who did investigations there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, place a line parallel to the street, with the number 8.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the benefit of the record, those last three markings were at J7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'd like to add that Ozrenska goes -- stretches all this way here and ends up here. So these are all the localities which are below Hrasno, Cengic Vila, Dolac Malta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, please place a line along number 6 for the relevant Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kucanin. Before we leave those three streets, are you able to tell us which streets received fire from those three streets, that's Ozrenska, Zagorska, and Milinkladska.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milinkladska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This street, Vojvoda something, this high street. I forget what it was called then. Now it's called Zamario [phoen]. Then Dzemala Bijedica. And these transfer streets, Ivana Krndelja. I knew it's name, on the other side, I mean it's called something else on the other side. Then Miljenka Cvitkovic Street. We talked about that incident yesterday. I just can't find it on the map now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please mark those streets which received fire from those three sources by blue lines, and then circle those streets, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Would you place a capital Z inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now please continue to locate other positions on the map, moving in a clockwise direction, which were identified from police investigations in the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my colleagues' reports, those who worked in Novi Grad, in the locality of Dobrinja, that is, from Dobrinja I. In that part, there was a street called -- now, I forget its name right now. Oh, yes. Miroslava Krleze. And a sniper fire was non-stop opened against the rest of Dobrinja, especially against the central part. That street, to my mind, could be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please draw a line parallel to the street.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And place a number 9 alongside it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the locality of Nedzarici, sniper fire was targeted at these three vertical streets, and the horizontal one, which linked the locality of Dobrinja with the rest of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate those streets again, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Olimpijska Street. This one I believe was called Prvomajska, and the next one, I don't know what it was called. And this one which was the worst one, as I could experience myself when I went to perform my duties there. It was really a hazard to go down this street, because it was constantly exposed to firearms, and that was non-stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part here, it is called Lukavicka Cesta, and this one, yes, it was Ante Babica. Yes, that's what it was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which part received sniper fire from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just as these three streets are, but those vertical. So from the first street Prvomajska to the point where you enter the locality of Dobrinja. So it's from here to here. That was the most exposed area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place a circle around the four streets that you have marked, and within the circle place capital letter Y.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please -- now, you've told us that you knew about Ante Babica Street from your own experience. What about the other three streets? Was that from your investigations or those of your fellow inspectors, or both?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assisted at an investigation here at the top of Provomajska Street, and as for the others, I told you that my brother lived here. And it was on the basis of what my colleagues said I mentioned those other two, and the third one, because the incidents there were quite high. I mean, they were frequent incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue. I'm sorry. Just before you leave that, would you place the number 10, I think it is, alongside, indicating Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do any investigation here, so it was on the basis of my colleagues' investigations from the Rajlovac barracks, and it was controlled by the army of Bosnian Serbs. So sniper fire was opened on the localities here and it's road. Now, that particular locality is called Sokolje, and it's here. You can read it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place the number 11 alongside the barracks, the position of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you mark the relevant streets which received fire, sniping fire, from that source.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a part of this locality of Sokolje. It is a very, very densely populated area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of some of those streets that received fire from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what they were called. All I know is that that particular locality is called Sokolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please mark that with capital letter X inside the circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my own experience, and yesterday we also talked about the Elma Jakupovic's murder, a little girl, and the sniper fire came from a place called Kromolj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark Kromolj with the number -- I think it's 12.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you place -- first of all, could you tell us the names of the areas that were targeted from sniping source number 12, Kromolj.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasana Brkica Street, and then the neighbourhood and the whole area of the sports -- the Kosevo sports stadium, Zetra sports hall, and then Djura Djakovica Street. That's it's old name. It's goes from [indiscernible] to Kobilja Glava, and the cemetery, the city cemetery, so the funerals couldn't take place because of snipers. So there was a rather wide area here which was exposed to sniper fair fire, or rather to firearms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the area of Kobilja Glava. Was that area, and indeed all of the areas you just mentioned, subjected to sniper fire from area 12 in the relevant period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please draw an outline of those areas that you have just mentioned that received fire from position 12.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be quite a large area. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place the capital letter W inside the circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, may I assume that since you're standing, that you'll start the cross-examination of Mr. Kucanin?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My colleague will start the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Is it correct that you gave a number of statements, in particular, on the 10th, and the 11th, and most probably the 12th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not receive interpretation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you now received interpretation? It seems that you have. Very well. Witness, in this statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should perhaps show the statement to the witness, in accordance with our practice, so that the witness could confirm his signature. I will show him only the first page, because other pages have been annotated by myself. The number, for the transcript, is the ERN number 00360864.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give the document back to the usher so that I can have it back myself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so we can therefore agree that you gave this particular statement, that you signed it. Now I should like to know whether it is correct that you stated that you were able to remember a certain number of incidents. Thanks to the fact that you have preserved all of the notes that you have made following these investigations, and that as a consequence you were able to provide the details of the incidents in question.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was possible for me to remember some of the events. The interview took place in 1995, so not long after the incidents. And some of the information I provided on the basis of my notes, which I made throughout the war while conducting my investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was as follows: Is it correct that in respect of each incident you had notes, and that you have kept these notes; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago you spoke about these notes, or this notebook. I should like to know, technically speaking, what form they are.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the agendas, where I described my duties as a police inspector on a daily basis. I would record the date of the incident and all other relevant steps that I took in connection with my work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. Are you still in possession of this notebook?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I am. I'm not sure whether I have them all. It was, after all, eight or ten years ago. But I think I have kept most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you haven't brought these notebooks or this notebook with you here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers be asked to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified some time ago about an incident, including a car which you took to the apartment where an investigating magistrate lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the English translator asked that the two speakers pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I was listening to the French channel, I couldn't hear it. Mr. Kucanin, could you please make a pause between the question put to you and the answer you give, since the interpreters have to translate everything you say and since Mr. Piletta-Zanin is able to follow the original language, it might go too quick. May I also ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to do the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Ierace, for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we were speaking about this notebook. Could you confirm for me whether it still exists or no? Did you say yes? Is it correct that it still exists?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't sure. I said that most of the agendas are probably still in existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. When I mentioned a moment ago the problems concerning the incident involving the investigating magistrate, you declared that it was not necessary that this incident be made part of the record. May I ask you why, in your opinion, this was not necessary?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I didn't conduct any official investigation on that occasion. I simply wanted to tell you a story and to describe you how we were able to establish the firing position on this occasion, in this particular area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how can you be sure that this incident took place in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I can, simply -- because I know when approximately the location was discovered as a sniper fire position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of the year was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was not wintertime. We were lightly dressed. We left the vehicle until nightfall there, and it was only after that we were able to pull it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you on that occasion? Were any colleagues with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of these individuals, if you remember. If you don't, just say so, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the judge that you were going to fetch?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zdenko Eterovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you've mentioned a vehicle in respect of this incident. What kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a police car, a police car, a Golf, which was painted blue and white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a Golf. Does it mean that the police at that time had Golfs as their vehicles? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry I have to ask this question. What was the gas station that the police normally used for refilling at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to any gas station to refill the fuel during the war in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not operational. There was no fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are telling us that it was not possible to obtain, normally, fuel in the town of Sarajevo at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to police cars and the way they obtained fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. However, you just told us that there was no longer any gas station in the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were gas stations. Whether they were working or whether civilians were able to obtain fuel on such stations, I don't know. I never went to any gas station during the war to refill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please confirm this for us, sir: Did you remain in Sarajevo throughout the war, that is, throughout the relevant period, from the beginning of the war up until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to your knowledge, the UNPROFOR personnel, did they have to -- did they need fuel for their vehicles, such as ambulances and official vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, as a police officer, were able to use an official vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My vehicle was a civilian one. It was also a Golf, which we referred to as Dvica, and it was painted red. It was a special type of Golf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this vehicle, did you normally drive it, this official vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the driver?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was an official vehicle which I drove whenever I was on duty, whenever I went out on the scene. The same case applied to others. I did not use this vehicle personally; it was at the disposal of my colleagues as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. However, throughout those three years of time, you never went to any gas station to refill this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I refilled it daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Where did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for each and every visit of the scene, I received a Coca-Cola bottle of fuel. But it was not always fuel. Sometimes it was oil for regular heaters, like fuel oil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer, Witness. Why didn't you buy fuel at a petrol station?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buy fuel? Are you forgetting that there was a war going on in Sarajevo? I just didn't have a penny in my pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but maybe it was possible for you to obtain some kind of cards or rations that you could have used directly at the petrol station, and I am referring to the institution, to the service whose employee you were. Did they give you any such thing?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, I received from my institution, from my work institution, a bottle, a litre and a half bottle of fuel. If the destination was far away, I got a bigger bottle. There were very severe restrictions, and Sarajevo, generally speaking, did not have fuel. But the police had some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You will told us that you didn't have money to buy fuel. I think that unfortunately that was the case for many persons. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this precision. I should now like to go back to some other incidents that you had experience of. In particular, I am interested in the incident which happened at the restaurant or in the vicinity of the restaurant whose name escapes me at the moment. Maybe Atina. That was the name of the restaurant, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was called then exactly. It seems to be that it was called Adrijana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're quite correct. The name of the restaurant was Adrijana. Sorry, I forgot the name. Let us focus now on this particular incident. I think you can remember the incident very well. You testified that you were there at the scene and that you were the most experienced police officer at the scene on that occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. You also told us that you had investigated the scene where the incident had taken place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I think that I can conclude from your previous statements that, as an experienced policeman, you issued immediate instructions to local police officers, if there was any on the location, in order to protect the scene of the incident, to seal the scene and to protect the traces of the incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When visiting the scene, the area -- I mean, the traces were preserved, but I don't remember whether the area was secured by the local police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But I was speaking of a general rule, general regulation. Normally, you said that you had also photographers who worked as members of your team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, these teams of photographers, is it correct that they participated in all such operations that you were called upon to perform?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said teams of photographers. Those were actually teams of so-called technicians, each of whom had a special duty during the investigation. Some were ballistics experts, for example, some were in charge of making a diagram of the scene and make photos of the scene. Those measures would be taken right away at the onsite investigation, whereas my duty as a lead of the onsite investigation, was to make sure that all the information relating to the incident is gathered, including the names of eyewitnesses, victims, if any, casualties, the wounded, the fatalities, and to describe, generally speaking, the measures taken as part of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about members of the team who performed several duties, but is it true that, first of all, you would take photographs of what had happened and then later on you would conduct the investigation? Was it the other way around? Did you first examine the scene and then take photographs? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, one would examine the scene of the incident in order to establish -- to find the traces of the incident. Once the traces are established, they are clearly marked with arrows or numbers. Afterwards, these traces are photographed, and that was the duty of the crime technician. Throughout that time, I'm doing my job. I'm conducting the investigation, waiting for them to finish their job. So each of us had their specific duty which was part of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in thinking that, chronologically speaking, before you touched anything on the scene, before you removed the traces on the scene, you would always take photographs so that that can be part of your file? Or was it the other way around? Would you take a bullet, examine it, and then put it back in situ and take photographs of it? Could you explain this to us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is never done the way you've just described it anywhere in the world, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mentioned two possibilities. The first one, first you take photographs and then you make an investigation, and the other one the other way around: First you do the investigation, you examine the scene, and then you take the photographs. Which is the wrong one?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, the crime -- I'm a crime technician and I know that traces on the scene of the incident cannot be removed or tampered with, in any way, before photographs are taken. That is what my colleagues do. Simultaneously, I conducted the investigation, trying to obtain information as to who the victims were, who the eyewitnesses were, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So first of all you take photographs, and then you proceed with the investigation; am I correct in understanding your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation starts from the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin [Previous translation continues]... Question several times, but it seems that you'd like to have either another answer or some other clarification which is not clear to me at all. So would you please put such a question that makes clear what you want the witness to tell you exactly, apart from that it's your usual answer is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be happy to do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... What you'd like to hear from the witness or otherwise proceed to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. I will be even clearer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 60, line 20, you told us that one cannot touch the traces on the scene of the incident before photographs are taken. That's what you said on page 60, at line 20, approximately; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't see this in the transcript. All I can tell you is -- I mean, I can only repeat what I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read English, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think if you include in the witness [sic] a reference to the transcript, the witness might be confused, because I don't see him look at the transcript. So I assume that he'll not follow it. And it's confusing for him if you refer to a transcript he doesn't know about. But apart from that, let me just make it clear. Mr. Kucanin, you testified that before taking photographs of the scene of the crime, including such objects as bullets, they should not be touched prior to taking photographs; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you were able to analyse a number of photographs given to you by the Prosecution in connection with Adrijana cafe. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at this point I should like to show you photographs number 00284 and 266.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the photographs to the witness, and I should like the witness to confirm whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: From Exhibit P2792?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's it, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go back to the previous one, please. Yes, that's the one. Witness, could you please confirm whether that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And perhaps we can put the photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm, Witness, that this is the awning, the canvas awning of the restaurant concerning this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, can we now have the photograph which is on -- which is two pages later in the document. The photograph depicts the impact of the bullet. Yes, that's the one. Can we please -- no, the other one, please, the one after that one. Yes, that's the one I need.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have a photograph here, 00284270, for the record. Is this the window that was hit by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please indicate on the photograph where the canvas awning was.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it on the photograph, because it was in front of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please go back to the previous photograph, then. You told us that this was the sunshade or the awning through which the bullet had passed before it hit the glass which is behind the awning. A moment ago you saw the photograph depicting the impact of the bullet in the glass, and in response to a question put to you by His Honour, Judge Orie, that no traces were touched -- no traces of the incident were touched before the investigation. I should like to go back to the previous photograph, and I should like you to tell us where, in relation to the bullet impact, was the sunshade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to the previous photograph, please, number -- [In English] that one. The right one. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you told us that traces were not touched. Can we see here the beginning of the sunshade?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, you can only see the side of the awning, which was not hidden by the bullet. That is, you can see the awning, but from the side. As far as this photograph is concerned, the awning would be in front of the cafe, that is, the part of the awning through which the bullet had passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the upper part of the photograph, can you see a long horizontal tube which was probably pulled up by a mechanism on the left part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are close to half past 12.00. If there would be a suitable moment for you to ... if you have one or two questions, then -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be a perfectly suitable moment, Your Honour, because we can continue with the photograph after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you one question before the break? I have with great interest followed your line of questioning. It's not quite clear to me, but perhaps you could give me a short explanation. Is it what you seek to establish that there is a contradiction between what the witness said about not touching any material found at the place of the scene before it would have been photographed, that no picture could have been taken from the window when the -- how do you call it in English -- when the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the sunshield was -- the word "awning." I was not that much aware of ... If the awning was still in place, or is there any specific reason why you ask, or is it just to establish that the awning had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm happy to tell you that, but if I say it in the presence of the witness, who is shaking his head, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Go, but since I heard a lot of questions which -- well, at the end of the specific part of the testimony, well, did not seem of great relevance to me, for example, whether other people would have pennies in their pocket as well compared to Mr. Kucanin. Well, I still -- I'm not aware to be -- to see exactly what -- if Mr. Kucanin says that he drove in a police Golf, the next question was whether the police had a Golf. Well, of course, if there's any reason to believe that there's anything wrong with his answer that the police would just have Volkswagens and not Golfs, I would perfectly understand your question. That's why I did not interfere. But if the witness answered that the police had Golfs, well, that was it. There was never any other answer. So it's still unclear to me whether you had in mind that there were other vehicles, that there were no Golfs used by the police. So I'm just -- during the break, perhaps, of 20 minutes, I invite you to think of the relevance not only of the subject you are touching but also the relevance of each individual question. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that you would like to bring something to my attention. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Very briefly. Simply, the Defence takes great care about the relevance of its questioning, and I want to say, this witness stated -- I will say it directly, because I think it is very important- that a certain tubing system was used to establish where -- from where the direction came. Now, if that tube was misplaced, then obviously all the measurements were wrong, and we need to ask this question. As for the questions about the petrol and the money, your Tribunal asked a question about a car, and we established that it was Golf. Now, what we want to know: Is it whether civilians could obtain petrol freely in Sarajevo, and if civilians could not do that -- and that's what I was asking the witness --- if they couldn't, then my question is: Who could drive these vehicles? Could it be civilians, since there was no petrol available to the civilians? And I think it is a fundamental question with regard to the bullets, to the projectiles which possibly hit -- which allegedly hit vehicles. So that is my question. When you say we are asking irrelevant questions, it is quite possible that the Defence may think -- may think, that this observation I will not say that it is -- I should say that such a comment, such a remark, may shake the Defence, may destabilise the Defence's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last thing I would like to do is to destabilise the Defence. I think it's not at this moment proper to start a debate on the relevance of the few examples I gave. And let me just -- yes. Perhaps, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, part of the problem is -- which I do not have it with your lead counsel, as you may have noticed --, if you perhaps come to your point a bit quicker. When I asked you what your line of questioning was aiming at, I gave an example, which, as far as I could imagine, might not be the aim you were seeking. I did that specifically in order not to interfere with the line of questioning. But if you come quicker to your point, and if you -- it's quite clear now and then that the witness gave a clear answer on not touching any objects found at the scene of the incident. It's really not necessary to ask him four times. Although I do understand that it's quite important for you to establish that this was his answer, but everyone heard it, and the second time he confirmed that we heard it again, and the third time we heard it again. So I think if you come quicker to your point, I'll be less inclined to intervene, as you might have noticed, in comparison with your -- the technique you use in cross-examining and your lead counsel. Of course, I'm not saying who is the best, you'll understand. But is this -- may I assume that this response to your remarks and that we can continue the cross-examination of Mr. Kucanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President. Thank you very much. There is absolutely no problem. I merely wished to -- wanted to clear up a point. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you then please bring in the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Kucanin. The cross-examination by Defence counsel will now continue. You did not have your earphones on yet. Cross-examination of the witness by Defence counsel will continue, but I think first Mr. Ierace wants to bring something to the attention of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I reserve just a minute or so at the end of today's session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for coming back into the courtroom. I'd like to go back to the photographs. They will be given you now. It is the same photographs that we had a moment ago on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, can you please show the first photograph, 266. Will you please place it on the ELMO. Very good. Witness, we can see this garden cafe. Can you please show us, by using the pointer, where -- from where exactly did the bullet strike, on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't do it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you generally point at the area which the bullet struck, the area of the canvas which was struck by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I'm not claiming it with full certainty, but I think it was this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now blow this up. Could we now blow up this area. And will you please try to focus it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might there be some recording for the transcript of where the witness indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please state for the transcript where the witness pointed at, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this entry point, you indicated that today you are not quite positive where is it that the bullet struck exactly.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After all this time, and on this photograph, no, I'm not -- I cannot be positive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, can we show 269, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin has not done it. I'm content to do it from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although the second answer of the witness was that he couldn't do it with great precision. But if you, for the sake of clarity of the transcript, of course, we could indicate where the earlier pointing at was. I think it was at the right portion, the first right portion, with some five half circles at the bottom of the awning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never seen so much assistance, and I am delighted. Thank you very much. Let us move on. Can we have photograph 4269, please, with the help of the usher, of course. Very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we see an arrow. Is it pointing at the entry point of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move, slightly, the image while preserving the blow-up, but moving slightly to the left. No, no, no. In the other direction. Left. A little bit more. Yes. Thank you very much. Thank you. Stop, please. Now, Witness, do you see here, please, a seam in the canvas which, in its lower part, falls down, a festoon I believe it is called, a festoon which descends on the lower part of the screen. I believe your answer was yes, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please give this back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you, then, usher, please take us back to the first photograph, 4266, and I want to ask the technical booth to again blow up the festoons, in particular -- no, no, no. The upper part, upper part. Here we see the table and chairs. Yes, this is the festoon area. And will you now move it a little bit to the left. There.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you see in this photograph -- can you find once again in this photograph -- you have the original before you, and I'd like to ask the technical booth -- there. Witness, can you identify here the seam which we indicated a moment ago which came down the centre of the festoon?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I think there are more of them here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Which end up directly in the centre of a festoon? I'm not quite sure. Could you make a backwards zoom now, please. Can you please -- the technical booth, can you please help us and make a backward zoom. I believe I need the Presidential intervention. Oh, yes. Thank you. And now, in the booth, can you focus on the area which is slightly above the neck of the person who appears in this photograph on the left-hand side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be zoomed in. That's what you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm kindly asking the booth to do that. A little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. And now a little bit to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A bit to the left, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There. There. There we are. More to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it enough, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was waiting for the camera to go to the place. And can we move a little bit more to the left, please. Now a bit to the right. No. This was to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's difficult for the usher --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I do understand this. [Interpretation] Here we are. Can we now zoom, blow up this particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want it more, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know whether it is technically possible, but if we look closely at the photograph that you have before you, then we clearly have this seam, the area of the seam, which goes down the axis of the entrance into the restaurant, and it is where this seam is, and it comes down to the centre of the festoon. Now, seemingly, it is where I'd like to focus, but if the technology that we have does not allow us to do it, we shall do it some other way. Obviously the technology does not allow us to focus on it, so I want to withdraw this document. And usher, will you please put once again 2670 on the screen. Here we are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for the transcript, we are talking about the photograph which does not show at all the canvas or the sunshade or whatever it might be. Now, Witness, on this photograph I see two, I would say two bullet impacting sites; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you right, you said two points of impact, did you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you well, I did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin asked you whether it's right that you see two impacts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. I see only one point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Would you please point on the screen which you have on your -- to the right, where is this point of impact that you see here?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So for the screen, the witness points at -- rather, at more or less a triangular point, which is in the second row and the second line, in the square which is the second from above and second from the left. Would you agree that that is a relatively large hole?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you placed a system of tubes between two points in order to establish the direction from which the bullet came. Would you agree that it would be between the point -- the entry point on the canvas and this point here?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. We see that there is no canvas on this photograph, so it may seem difficult. But insofar as the impact produced a relatively large hole, how did you -- what did you then do to establish precisely the direction from which the bullet impacted the glass?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph you do have the canvas except that it is dark. If you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you see here the robe which ties the canvas to the metal frame and it is a permanent contraption, so -- and it is closer to the window shop. I cannot agree with what you said. This canvas was tied here all the time. So what did we do, then? We had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Witness. I'm talking only about the hole that we see here in this photograph. Sorry to interrupt you. This is -- and you tell us that this is a relatively large hole. You also said that at times you used a very small tube so as to identify the origin of the bullet. And what I'm asking you about is: When you have such a large hole, what do you do then to regulate this tube, if you want to establish the direction? Because the hole, the opening, is so large.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the enclosed you can see that -- I'm an inspector. I'm not a ballistics expert. I'm no expert at all in matters of ballistic. I am repeating to you what I see technicians do. Yesterday I described a contraption which we call the Vizir or Smeker, and which our experts used to establish the direction. This tube had at the end something like an antenna, like this thing that I have in my hand. They could extend it. And in the middle there was a tube, and above it there was a small periscope-like device. I understand what you are saying, that the hole was large, but by centering this device in the middle of the hole and then linking it with the other hole, one could establish the part of the bullet exactly. I can tell you, on the basis of this glass, if you have only one hole, and I can describe to you how one can establish the bullet path on the basis of one hole. I can do it even though I say this is not my job. I'm merely an inspector who conducts the investigation, and it is up to others to do their job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. I've understood that you are not an expert, but can you tell us, please, what is vertically -- what is at a distance one kilometre an arrow angle of about 10 degrees on a vertical elevation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you what such an arrow means, but the distance here in this particular case could have been about 200 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. You told us that you were not an expert, but nevertheless every time that such an incident happens, and when you investigated, you tell us there was always a ballistic expert on site, on the scene of the crime. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, I'd like to show this witness a document which came from the Prosecution, which is ERN 00234308. We have a copy also for interpreters. It is an exhibit which has -- premarked Exhibit P2790, and in brackets it says [Previous translation continues]... Shall I repeat the number? Because you did not hear me. 2790, and 2791.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a sufficient number of copies, and I should like to ask the usher to take them and distribute them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Copies for the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet, Mr. President, but there will be very little translation for once, which will spare us some problems, at least as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, there is a document in front of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have in front of you a document 00234308? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is this a report that you prepared?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an official note made by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did it concern an incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this document, which will be tendered, can you tell us where we can find the name of the ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this official note that I made, no names need to be mentioned, not necessarily. In this case, I was just an investigation assistant, because I had received information that one person had been killed, and that was the reason why I visited the scene. When I established that the person in question was only wounded, the investigation was taken over by my colleague from the relevant police station, in this case, the police station of Novo Sarajevo, and he made the official report, which contains all relevant information, including the names of persons who participated in the investigation. In this official note, I only make mention, general mention, of the incident that occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We will perhaps go back to this document shortly. For the time being, I should like to address the issue of circumstances of the incident, and I need some precision. What was the child doing at the moment she [as interpreted] was hit?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what we knew at the time, from what the witnesses told us, the child was either riding a bicycle or pushing a wheel near the wall of a building there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this, I should like to know whether the child was accompanied by his parents.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you now tell us what was the approximate distance between the alleged firing position, that is, the position from which the bullet had come, and the location of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, two or three hundred metres. The terrain is not even in this area. It was a hilly terrain. And the fire was opened from a hill, so I couldn't tell you what the exact distance was. However, I must say that I don't see the relevance of this question, because a child is a child, and must not be targeted, whatever happens, even if he were near the trenches.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand your remark, sir, concerning this event, but I need some further precision. What did this child wear? What kind of clothing did he have on?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. We didn't find him on the scene. It was only at the hospital that we saw the child, and that is, after all, what you can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You conducted this investigation, sir, but you failed to ask [as interpreted] what kind of clothing this child was wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done by the inspector who was the leader of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that inspector?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember. Very well. I understand. Who was the ballistics expert for this particular incident? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this document. It must have been Senad Mesic, one of the most experienced ballistics experts in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will wind up with this incident. Since the witness told us he couldn't remember, I should like to now go back to the Alipasino Polje incident. Sir, yesterday, in response to a question by the Presiding Judge, you said that you remembered very well that there was a kind of headquarters, a military headquarters, in the area of Alipasino Polje. I should like to take you back to this incident, because we need some further precision. Do you know the address of the place that you mention, or rather, mentioned in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I was not able to tell you the exact location because I couldn't remember. I told you it was some kind of an administrative unit, but now I know that it was a personnel department. I made some effort and I managed to remember what it was. So it was the personnel department of the Kulin Ban unit, which unit, to my knowledge, didn't have any specific positions. I don't know what kind of unit it was. All I know, that later on when we fought some internal crime incident, which is known to all that -- at the end of 1993 the Ministry of the Interior made some actions to that effect. So it was a department which was some 200 metres away from the point of impact on Rade Koncara Square in the Alipasino Polje neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let's stay with this incident for a while. This is very important information for the Defence. I would like to know whether you managed to remember this here in The Hague, whether it was here that you remembered this unit.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only the name of the unit, but the very existence of a military facility in the region.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it was targeted. In my report, or in my official note, I also stated the name, Kulin Ban, of the unit, but I must say that we never shrunk from mentioning something that we thought was important. If you're doing your job professionally, there is no reason to hide anything. I understand what you want to establish. You want to establish that the gentlemen from the other side were targeting this military facility but somehow ended up killing three and wounding 20 civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, well, you perhaps know things that I don't know, but I would like to know, in which document precisely you indicated the existence of this military facility at the time of the investigation. In your report, where do you make mention of that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My official report was made on the scene of the incident, so upon the onsite investigation, I made record of this piece of information. As I said, there was a whole team of people, and their names are contained in this report, together with the names of the casualties, the killed, the wounded, and eyewitnesses with, if you have the report in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the official note 19/05-2, dated 22nd of July, 1994 do you remember that? I'm sorry. 10th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the exact reference, but I remember that a document was made which is called an official report on that date, and that the incident took place in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My colleague will go back to this issue, because she is better familiar with the geography of the place. Let me ask you whether it is correct that in this report you make mention of the fact that there was a military factory on this locality.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Let us go back to this military facility that we mentioned. You said that it was involved with personnel issues. Do you know how many people worked in this facility?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, no. I don't think it is a very significant number. I don't think that anyone wore a uniform there. Mostly women worked there. Your colleague is probably familiar with the area, so she must know how large this square is, this tarmac square between these buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, didn't you state in one of your statements that it is possible that at that moment of time, several civilians wearing uniform may have passed at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember stating something of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't state that? Very well. I take note of that. So there was absolutely no one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Since my learned colleague has put to this witness that he stated in one of his statements that it is possible that at that moment several civilians wearing uniforms passed, I'd ask that he identify the statement by the date and the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, are you able to quote literally?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'll be happy to do it in a moment. I will look for it. I think it's in the Serb text. And we'll go back to the issue when we find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us now continue with the geographical layout, the location of this incident. Was this facility on the ground floor or upstairs?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know where it was. I never saw it. It is just on the basis of statements given by eyewitnesses that we conducted our investigation, and they told us that the shell tail was lying somewhere around. So we were busy looking for this tail. However, if you're basing yourself on the statement, I wish I had given a statement to the effect that a soldier was passing by, and if anyone was able to see a soldier passing by in a square in the Nedzarici neighbourhood, together with 500 other civilians, I mean, if such a person -- such an individual could be targeted, then that must be an expert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You raised an issue involving a shell. Do you know what happened with that shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that a shell exploded and killed civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are you not aware of the fact that some parts of this shell, in particular, the tail, is perhaps in the possession of the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now asking me about the parts of the shell, but a moment ago you asked me about the shell in its entirety. Now, this a different thing. On the basis of fragments that we were able to find at and around the point of impact, one can easily establish what kind of projectile that was. As for the tail, it was no longer on the -- at the spot of -- at the very spot, at the impact spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question. Do you know whether this very important part of the shell, which is called the tail, is in the possession of the army? Do you know if they have this part of the shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have read my report, you would see that the tail was -- or the stabiliser, as you call it, was taken by the members of such-and-such unit. I don't remember the name of the unit. So we did not find it on the spot. We found all other parts of the shell, on the basis of which we could determine the type of the shell. As for the tail, we didn't find it. Whether it was found subsequently, I don't know, but I know that when we came to the scene, we started to search for the tail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I may have read your report, but the Chamber hasn't, and that is why I have to put to you these questions, because the Chamber is not familiar with your report. Speaking of the stabiliser, or rather, the tail, it seems that the army gathered the traces of the incident. Does it mean that before your arrival, members of the army had already been there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. If members of the army had not been there, would the members of your team have found this part of the debris?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once it happened, for instance, that children took the -- one of such traces from the scene of the incident. It's not necessarily the army. You have to understand the way it happened. This one shell fell right after the other. There was war going on in Sarajevo. One was -- one could risk death at every corner, at every moment, in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that nobody was there before you. I think that we should read your testimony yesterday. I think that -- it was the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have not worked on the revised version of the text but on the original that we had, and as a result of that, the line that I am about to give can only be the hour. So it was 10 hours, 0016.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin's question starts with the words: "Witness, you told us that nobody was there before you." That is not my reading of the evidence the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this line where you're referring to yesterday's testimony, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, which we tried to locate?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't understand the question that you asked. I was just checking something else on my screen. Would you be please so kind and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace made an objection against the first part of your question, which appears on page 83, line 18, which reads: "Witness, you told us that nobody was there before you. I think that we should read your testimony yesterday. I think it was the 28th." Since Mr. Ierace tells us that in his recollection that was not the testimony given and since you were referring to yesterday, I wondered whether this first line of your question referred to yesterday's testimony you're just trying to locate. So the testimony that nobody was there before the witness; would that be yesterday's testimony or would it be of today? But I have another solution, perhaps. Mr. Ierace asked us for one minute before the break -- before we adjourn until tomorrow. This will give ample opportunity to Mr. Piletta-Zanin to see whether he can find the source of this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but what I can tell you right away, there seems to have been a misunderstanding. I can tell you right away, because I wish to be perfectly loyal, that the spot where the witness mentioned was at 10 hours, 15, when he mentioned a soldier as being part of this group. Do you want to -- do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have it in front of you, perhaps we could -- yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm using yesterday's transcript, without any times in it, as it appears on my computer, so that's the reason why I couldn't immediately locate 10.00. Please read the line, and perhaps then we'll put the question to the witness tomorrow, But we'll at least have located what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read what I see in the transcript, 10 hours, 16: "[In English] [Previous translation continues]... may have passed by, but there was no military formation there."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think your -- let me just have a look. Is the difference in view, Mr. Ierace, that the text just read by Mr. Piletta-Zanin is that "may have passed by," where his question today - but I have to change to today's transcript - would be that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The words were: "Witness, you told us that no one was there before you." Now, those words bear no relationship to the part of the transcript which Mr. Piletta-Zanin has just read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps, since we have to continue anyway tomorrow, could we just try to think it over? We've got some time for it. And then I'll now give an opportunity to Mr. Ierace to make a remark. He said he would use one minute. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I would have finished it easily if I would not have the fear that this courtroom might be needed this afternoon. That's always the morning session that has to end timely. If this would -- please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I'm about to say actually relates to this witness, but I don't think that there will be a problem. I'm informed through the Victims and Witnesses Unit that this witness is most anxious to return to Sarajevo by tomorrow night. He travels by train. It's a two-day trip to return. He's been here for two weeks waiting to give his evidence and giving his evidence, and he now faces serious concerns on the part of his employer, to the point that he fears that his employment may be in some jeopardy if he doesn't return. I draw that to the Trial Chamber's attention in the hope that we are at least able to finish this witness's evidence tomorrow. I don't blame anyone, of course. I've taken some considerable time in examination-in-chief. I had hoped that the map-marking would reduce it. But it's simply an unavoidable problem that we have a little backlog. Of course, Mr. Harding is waiting around as well. So, Mr. President, the reason I raise the issue is simply to clarify whether we could expect that cross-examination will finish by, say, the -- halfway through the last session tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Halfway through the last session, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That would allow some little time for any re-examination and questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Yes. Of course, we cannot give an answer to your question at this very moment, since we still have to wait to -- well, how the cross-examination develops. Mr. Piletta-Zanin or Ms. Pilipovic, could you give an estimate on whether you would be able, well, let's say, to finish the cross-examination tomorrow by -- it would then be approximately a quarter past 1.00 or shortly after 1.00? That would mean that you have another -- let's say a little bit over three hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we'll do our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's commitment we have to accept. Mr. Kucanin, we heard about -- you see that we paid attention to your problems and you had to wait here for quite a long time, which is, well, beyond our control. But we'll resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
